newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end at record high again.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end at record high again.

text.p: A Dow-inspired Australian share market ended at its second-straight record close on Tuesday although early gains were nearly wiped-out late in the session by profit-taking and a fall in the shares of Rupert Murdoch's international media company, News Corp.

The key All Ordinaries index closed 2.9 points higher at 2,366.2, well off its intra-day and life-time high of 2,380.8. The December share price index ended down seven points at 2,384 and at a 17.8 point premium to the underlying index.
News Corp's fall came after the company told its annual meeting its first quarter earnings were expected to be below expectations.

Peter Struk, a dealer at Sydney brokerage Reynolds and Co, said News Corp chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch's speech at the company's annual meeting in Adelaide caused a noticeable shift in sentiment for the stock.
"Without a doubt, Murdoch's comments knocked the stock down over the day on a considerable amount of volume," Struk said.
He said the market was concerned that weakness in the first quarter could flow to the company's second quarter results.
News Corp shares ended 14 cents weaker at A$7.20 (US$5.70).
Dealers said the remainder of the market was mixed to firmer with major resource issues BHP and WMC ending with modest gains and the key bank sector posting a solid rise on the day.

Topping the turnover list on Tuesday was engineering group National Consolidated which saw about 19 percent of its issued capital traded. Adelaide Steamship Group announced after the close that it had sold its approximate 15 percent stake.
The shares of transport group TNT were also active with the company's suitor, Dutch postal and telecoms group KPN, lifting its stake to 14.9 percent from 9.9 percent.
In other trade, building materials and sugar refining group CSR's stock ended lower after the company warned the market that its first half earnings were likely to fall by about 20 percent.
CSR shares closed 11 cents down at A$4.42.
